evidence.claim: Its later change of number was tied to Branson’s entertainment strip: to let the city take over the stretch between Route 376 and US 65, the state rerouted Route 76 along the Highroad and US 65.
evidence.quote: In order for the city of Branson to obtain the "strip" of Branson between Route 376 and US 65, Route 76 was routed on to the Highroad and US 65 between the Highroad and 76 Country Boulevard.

evidence.claim: Route 465 was decommissioned, and replacement of the old signs began on January 6, 2020.
evidence.quote: As Route 76 was re-aligned on to the entirety of the highroad, Route 465 was decommissioned. Work to replace the old signage started on January 6, 2020

evidence.claim: Marvel Cave came before Silver Dollar City, the 1880s-themed park that opened on May 1, 1960.
evidence.quote: Silver Dollar City opened on May 1, 1960. The park is an 1880s-themed experience.

evidence.claim: The park occupies the site of the older cave attraction, off Route 76 on Table Rock Lake’s Indian Point peninsula.
evidence.quote: The park is located off of Missouri Route 76 on the Indian Point peninsula of Table Rock Lake.

evidence.claim: The park occupies the site of the older cave attraction
evidence.quote: Silver Dollar City is located at the site of one of the Ozarks' oldest attractions, Marvel Cave.

evidence.claim: William Henry Lynch and his family began cave sightseeing operations in 1894.
evidence.quote: The Lynches began operation of the sightseeing venture on October 18, 1894.

evidence.claim: As automobile visitors arrived, Lynch cleared a path from Branson toward the cave that became Route 76.
evidence.quote: He cut brush and cleared a path for what would become Missouri Route 76

evidence.claim: As automobile visitors arrived, Lynch cleared a path from Branson toward the cave
evidence.quote: To accommodate the new influx of visitors traveling to the cave by car, Lynch was determined to bring a road from Branson to the cave.

evidence.claim: The Herschends later built an 1880s-style village above the cave, creating the themed town from which the park grew.
evidence.quote: Mary, Jack, and Peter began building an 1880s-style Ozark village on the surface surrounding the site of the cave.

evidence.claim: The original village included five shops, a church and a log cabin when it opened.
evidence.quote: The themed frontier town was named Silver Dollar City and originally was the site of five shops, a church, a log cabin

evidence.claim: Chula Vista is a 1,302-foot summit beside Route 248 at Buchanan Road in Taney County.
evidence.quote: Chula Vista is a summit in Taney County in the U.S. state of Missouri. The summit has an elevation of 1,302 feet (397 m). The summit lies along Missouri Route 248 at the intersection with Buchanan Road

evidence.claim: Its name came from a settler who had visited Chula Vista, California, and borrowed the name for this Missouri hill. In Spanish, it means pretty view.
evidence.quote: Chula Vista was named after Chula Vista, California, by a settler who had visited the city. The name is Spanish for "pretty view".
